name: Sam Rivera
headline: Trinity College senior, computer science. Looking for a first software job in 2027.

projects.name: Ask the course (RAG over course notes)
projects.what: A command-line program that indexes the course's Markdown pages with OpenRouter embeddings and answers questions from the top-scoring chunks.
projects.why: Python, because the course examples were Python and the cosine math is clearer there; text-embedding-3-small because it was the cheapest model that passed the five-question eval.
projects.breaks: Questions whose answer is spread across three pages: the top-three chunks miss one of them.
projects.learned: The index had 165 chunks and a query cost under a tenth of a cent; the retrieval, not the model, decided the answer quality.

projects.name: Receipt reader
projects.what: A vision model reads a photographed receipt into JSON and the code checks that the items add up.
projects.why: Two class models compared on seven receipts; the checker is plain code so the model's arithmetic is never trusted.
projects.breaks: A discount printed as a negative number; every model copied the sign and the total failed.
projects.learned: Edge cases are specification questions, not model bugs.

skills_shipped: OpenRouter chat, embeddings, vision, and image APIs

not_yet.why: No project has needed more than one server; I would learn it on the job.
The portfolio site is static HTML on purpose; a framework is on the list for the spring.
